review_scope: Renderer-backed close-range review of the project-owned Type-V rescue-PFD and river-helmet upgrade over five packaged CC0 guide and crew bodies.

assertions_include: substantial foam, webbing, buckle, helmet-shell, rim, and retention geometry exists on every avatar
five packaged CC0 bodies and zero Manny fallbacks remain active
aimed rescue paths, flexible fabric condition, and runtime rescue loop remain functional
all crew visual transforms remain finite

accepted_findings: The PFD now has tapered front flotation cells, a high back, fitted side wings, shoulder foam, a centre closure, two chest-adjustment runs, multiple buckles, and a lash tab instead of two isolated capsule-like pads.
PFD textile frequency is calibrated to an approximately 3 mm ripstop grid over the 30 cm panel scale, with reduced normal amplitude to remove the rejected sub-millimetre guide-camera shimmer.

The river helmet now has an open brow-length shell, temple and occipital coverage, an aligned edge rim, chin retention, top vent inserts, and separate charcoal crew versus brown guide material selection.
The equipment remains deterministic, project-owned, draw-call batched by material layer, compatible with all rescue poses, and independent of the D4-authoritative flexible-raft deformation path.
rejected_findings: The PFD and helmet are still parametric procedural geometry rather than scanned or artist-authored production PPE, and their close-range silhouette/body integration remains visibly synthetic.
The CC0 heads, generic wetsuits, omitted hair, and limited facial nuance remain below final photoreal character quality.
The procedural raft and flat test-tank background remain unsuitable for marketing or store media.
No named art director, qualified guide, product owner, legal reviewer, or release-media reviewer has approved this frame.
decision: Retain the upgraded safety gear as the deterministic playable fallback and production-body overlay. Do not close the M9 photoreal character, PPE, raft-art, named-review, or release-media gates. Replace or explicitly approve the assets through named review, then repeat this renderer test.
